staffing_team.text: 34 Back to Top 1. PROJECT INFORMATION This section provides an overview of the project. 1.1. PROJECT SUMMARY This project will be based on the scope of work template for the national courthouse hardening program. The contract work incorporates site demolition, asphalt pavement, concrete pavement, curbs, fencing, gates, landscaping, storm draining, windows & security glazing, security systems and electrical work. See Section 2.1 for detailed project requirements. The Contractor shall coordinate work and gain approvals required in this Statement of Work (SOW) with the Contracting Officer (CO) and Contracting Officer’s Representative/Project Manager (COR/PM) as required. 1.2. PROJECT BACKGROUND This asset, built in 1974, is comprised of a Seven-story office building and an attached three-story courthouse with full basement. The building is of masonry and steel construction containing 225,291 RSF. This asset has a multitude of tenants, with the major tenants being the, U.S. District Court, U.S. Bankruptcy Court, and DEA. This asset is located within the CBD for the City of Rochester. 1.3. CONTRACT TYPE This contract is a firm-fixed price contract. The services required shall include, but shall not be limited to, the following: ● Contract Management ● Construction Services

○ Notification appliance circuit calculations including voltage drop, circuit capacity, amplifier capacity, and power supply capacity. ○ Battery calculations for both the alarm and supervisory power requirements. Ampere- ¬hour requirements for each system component shall be submitted with the calculations. ○ Provide a color code schedule for the wiring and floor plans showing the location of all devices and equipment. ○ The signature and seal of a licensed Professional Fire Protection Engineer, or a NICET Level III or IV Technician. ● Prior to installation the contractor shall coordinate and schedule a fire alarm outage with the GSA project manager or GSA facilities management office. When work is being performed on an active fire alarm circuit(s), the fire alarm system must be taken out of service by the O&M vendor or their designated representative. The fire alarm system shall be returned to “normal” operating condition before the contractor and subcontractor(s) leave for the work shift. ● Fire alarm programming changes are permitted only when confirmed acceptance testing is scheduled with the AHJ or their designated representative. A fire alarm program change must be acceptance accepted within 24 hours of the change. The AHJ is the GSA regional fire protection engineer. ●

QUALITY CONTROL PLAN The Contractor shall develop, provide, and maintain a Quality Control Plan during the construction initiation of the project, based upon the USACE Three-Phases of Control, to accomplish the contract requirements. The Quality Control Plan shall identify personnel, procedures, instructions, records and forms to be used in carrying out the requirements of the Project. With respect to such information, Offerors shall agree to the terms as a condition of receipt such information, as set forth in this clause. This clause applies to all recipients of CUI building information (which falls within the CUI Physical Security category), including offerors, bidders, awardees, contractors, subcontractors, lessors, suppliers and manufacturers. Marking CUI: Contractors must submit any contractor-generated documents that contain building information to GSA for review and identification of any CUI building information that may be included. In addition, any documents GSA identifies as containing CUI building information must be marked in accordance with the Order and the Marking Controlled Unclassified Information Handbook (the current version may be found at https://www.archives.gov/files/cui/20161206-cui-marking-handbook-v1-1.pdf) before the original or any copies are disseminated to any other parties. If CUI content is identified, the CO ma

the original documents and all copies, before any dissemination, or authorized GSA employees may mark the documents. 1. Authorized recipients: a. Building information designated as CUI must be protected with access strictly controlled and limited to those individuals having a Lawful Government Purpose to access such information, as defined in 32 C.F.R. § 2002.4(bb). Those with such a Lawful Government Purpose may include Federal, state and local government entities, and non-governmental entities engaged in the conduct of business on behalf of or with GSA. Non-governmental entities may include architects, engineers, consultants, contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, utilities, and others submitting an offer or bid to GSA, or performing work under a GSA contract or subcontract. Recipient contractors must be registered as “active” in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at www.sam.gov, and have a Lawful Government Purpose to access such information. The existing HVAC systems have exceeded their useful life and must be replaced. Under this Design‑Build contract, the Contractor shall provide all professional design services, engineering, permitting, equipment selection, construction labor, materials, tools, and testing required to remove the existing HVAC systems and design/build a new fully integrated, energy‑efficient HVAC system compatible with the building’s layout and ductwork. Design an HVAC system meeting current industry standards, Washington State building codes, energy efficiency requirements (minimum 19+ SEER), and the operational needs of the facility. d. Develop construction drawings, technical specifications, product data sheets, and submittals for Government approval prior to construction. e. Provide design justification demonstrating that the proposed system meets required capacity, efficiency, and performance criteria. f. Remove existing HVAC components in accordance with environmental and hazardous material regulations. g. Construct and install the new HVAC system per the approved design package. h. Commission the completed system, perform airflow balancing, leak checks, refrigerant charging, testing, and final tuning. i. Deliver O&M manuals, warranty documentation, test results, and conduct onsite training for facility personnel. DESIGN-BUILD SCOPE OF WORK The Contr

deliverables_scope.text: operates ship and tow simulation capabilities in support of USACE navigation, coastal, and hydraulics missions. ERDC requires a contracting framework to augment its maritime simulation capabilities through collaboration with qualified entities outside the USACE. The contemplated requirement may be structured as a MATOC. Task orders may require support for ship simulation studies, simulator database development, vessel modeling, environmental modeling, visual database development, simulation testing, data analysis, technical documentation, training, simulator design support, software/hardware integration, and technical support. 3. Anticipated Scope of Work The contractor shall be capable of providing non-personal services to support ERDC ship, tow, and watercraft simulation activities. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to, the following: a. Maritime Simulation Study Support The contractor shall be capable of defining project problem sets and solution parameters; planning and conducting simulation studies; supporting feasibility and Pre-Construction Engineering and Design level studies; coordinating with professional mariners; and supporting ERDC oversight of simulation testing. b. Simulator Database Development The contractor shall demonstrate experience developing maritime si

et; Model validation using field data and professional mariner participation; and Delivery of databases, models, and project-specific data to the Government. c. Simulation Testing and Analysis The contractor shall be capable of conducting simulation testing to evaluate navigation designs, vessel maneuvering, safety, and operational feasibility. Analysis may include vessel track plots, heat maps, throttle and rudder usage, tug usage, maneuver feasibility, and safety assessments. d. Technical Reports and Documentation The contractor shall be capable of preparing, authoring, developing, and editing technical reports, project documentation, task requirements, software/hardware requirements, training materials, multimedia materials, web-based documentation, and other deliverables in support of ERDC simulation studies. e. Simulator System Support The contractor shall be capable of supporting ship/tow simulator hardware and software systems, including system assessments, hardware/software vetting, network architecture, installation, integration, validation, system optimization, maintenance, updates, refreshes, replacement, and technical troubleshooting. f. award_criteria.text: nufacturing capabilities. Authorized under DFARS Subpart 212-70, this CSO enables the Department of the Army to competitively procure solutions through a streamlined acquisition process, allowing for rapid award decisions. This approach underscores our mission to expedite the award and delivery of critical technologies, ensuring that the Army can leverage advancements in manufacturing swiftly and efficiently. By prioritizing speed in our contracting efforts, we aim to support the timely integration of cutting-edge technologies that enhance operational readiness. Contracts or agreements awarded under this authority will be structured as fixed-price, including fixed-price incentive fee contracts. Through this initiative, the Army reaffirms its commitment to fostering innovation and enhancing manufacturing operations, ultimately delivering superior capabilities to our warfighters. CSO Procedure: ACC-DTA seeks to award the following, but is not limited to: FAR contracts under FAR Part 12, Commercial Procedures; or non-FAR agreements such as transaction agreements under 10 U.S.C 4022; and Cooperative Agreements under 31 U.S.C. 6305 for ACC-DTA and/or its customers that are directly relevant to enhancing the effectiveness of development, integration, demonstration, and sustainment of ground vehicle systems capabilities to support Army modernization priorities and improve readiness. This CSO may result in awards to proposals for innovative, commercial technologies through multi-phased, competitive processes throughout 2028. The Government reserves the right to extend this CSO beyond the open until date by amendment if the authority is extended. The facility provides medical, dental, laboratory, radiology, pharmacy, and community health services. Routine waste removal services are required to maintain a clean, safe, and environmentally compliant healthcare environment that supports uninterrupted clinical operations. 3.0 Scope of Work The Contractor shall furnish solid waste collection and recycling services, including the rental, servicing, collection, transportation, and lawful disposal of solid waste and recyclable materials generated at Government facilities. Services shall include weekly collection of all designated containers and disposal of waste in accordance with all applicable Federal, State, Tribal, and local environmental regulations. The Government may request additional non-recurring waste collection services for construction debris or similar materials on an as-needed basis. 4.0 Performance Requirements The Contractor shall: Provide all waste and recycling
